source.note: Search summary: 36 courses (about 40% beginner slopes); lift system 20 (2 gondolas, 6 quad, 3 triple and 8 pair chairlifts, 1 surface lift) — a Wikipedia figure whose vintage is unclear; longest run 10 km from the summit. Area 297 ha; piste km not stated
Piste reference data — confirm at source. Only features Piste is confident about are set; everything else is unknown (null), not 'not offered'. The hot-spring village sits at the foot of the slopes

character: A traditional hot-spring village in northern Nagano whose ski area climbs three ridges to the 1,650 m summit of Mt. Kenashi, with a 10 km longest run. The village's free public baths and its January fire festival are part of its character.
learning: About 40% of courses are beginner slopes (search summary). Reference, confirm: ski schools (including English-language lessons) and rentals operate in the village.

transfers.name: Hokuriku Shinkansen to Nagano (or Iiyama), then bus to Nozawa Onsen
transfers.notes: Usually reached by Hokuriku Shinkansen from Tokyo (or Ueno) to Nagano, about 1.5 h, then by bus. Reference, confirm 2026-27 timetables and fares. Buses run from Nagano station; Iiyama, the next Shinkansen stop, is closer, with a shuttle bus (the Nozawa Onsen Liner) of about 25 min.

transfers.name: Shared shuttles from the Tokyo airports
transfers.notes: Reference, confirm: seasonal shared shuttles have run from Haneda and Narita. Operators and fares are not on file.
